chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about the prayer of the eclipse, and whether there is a make-up (qada) upon the one who leaves it. He said: 'If it passes you by, then there is no make-up upon you.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified the reasoning in examples of these two narrations, and the summary is that if the entire disk [of the sun] is eclipsed, make-up is obligatory upon the one for whom the eclipse prayer passes by; and if it is not entirely eclipsed and it passes him by, there is no make-up upon him. And there is no contradiction between the narrations, and this does not contradict what Ammar al-Sabati narrated in the narration we presented earlier from his saying: 'Make-up is only obligatory upon the one who was informed but did not pray until it passed him by,' because the reasoning in this narration is to interpret it as referring to when part of the disk is eclipsed and he was negligent in praying, then at that time make-up becomes obligatory upon him. And we only exempted make-up for the one who did not know about the partial eclipse at all. And upon this, the narrations are harmonized and do not differ.
ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to make up the eclipse prayer if one misses it?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* resolves apparent contradictions in Shia jurisprudence regarding the make-up (*qada*) of the eclipse prayer by distinguishing between total and partial eclipses alongside the element of negligence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that no make-up is required if the eclipse passes unnoticed, while the commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarifies that obligation arises only when the eclipse is total and the individual was informed but delayed. This harmonizes various reports by linking the legal duty to both the magnitude of the celestial event and the worshiper's awareness.
